Age-specific fertility rates (ASFR)

Source: R/indicators.R
age_specific_fertility_rate.Rd

Computes age-specific fertility rates per province, year, and single year of mother's age, following INE's methodology for its Indicadores Demograficos Basicos (INE, Indicadores Demograficos Basicos: Metodologia, pp. 4 and 9-10):

age_specific_fertility_rate(
  births_age_df,
  pop_df,
  age_min = 15L,
  age_max = 49L
)

Arguments

births_age_df

Tibble as returned by get_ine_births_by_age()$data (columns nuts3_code, province_name, year, age, female, total, and optionally age_group).

pop_df

Population tibble as returned by get_ine_population()$data (columns nuts3_code, year, age, female), January-1 stocks.

age_min, age_max

Integer bounds of the reproductive age span (default 15-49).

Value

A tibble with nuts3_code, province_name, year, age, births, women (mean annual female population), asfr (births per woman), asfr_female (female births per woman, for gross_reproduction_rate() and net_reproduction_rate()), asfr_per_1000 (1000 * asfr, for display), and is_boundary_year.

Details

  • Exposure is the mean annual female population, the average of the January-1 stocks of years t and t + 1. If the t + 1 stock is not in pop_df, the t stock is used and the row is flagged with is_boundary_year = TRUE (with a warning).

  • Out-of-range births are folded into the boundary ages: births to mothers younger than age_min (including INE's "under 15" group, coded age = NA, age_group = "under15") are added to age age_min, and births to mothers older than age_max (INE's "50 and over") to age age_max. No births are dropped.

Examples

births_age <- tibble::tibble(
  nuts3_code = "ES111", province_name = "A Coruna", year = 2023,
  age = c(20, 30), female = c(10, 25), total = c(20, 50)
)
pop <- tibble::tibble(
  nuts3_code = "ES111", year = rep(2023:2024, each = 2), age = c(20, 30, 20, 30),
  female = c(2000, 2500, 2100, 2400)
)
age_specific_fertility_rate(births_age, pop)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 10
#>   nuts3_code province_name  year   age births women    asfr asfr_female
#>   <chr>      <chr>         <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1 ES111      A Coruna       2023    20     20  2050 0.00976     0.00488
#> 2 ES111      A Coruna       2023    30     50  2450 0.0204      0.0102 
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: asfr_per_1000 <dbl>, is_boundary_year <lgl>
